environment.description: AWS Lambda (Quarkus native) behind API Gateway with Lambda authorizer that injects X-Tenant-Id from JWT claims (overwriting any client-supplied value). Lambda execution role uses dynamodb:LeadingKeys condition with substitution variable ${aws:PrincipalTag/TenantId} scoped to the partition key prefix. STS session tags are propagated from the Cognito identity pool's role mapping with tag key 'TenantId'. The IAM policy condition uses dynamodb:LeadingKeys to restrict GetItem to items where PK begins with TENANT#${aws:PrincipalTag/TenantId}. Note: the cache poisoning vector still exists in-process but the DynamoDB response will only ever contain data belonging to the authenticated tenant's partition, so a poisoned cache entry from Tenant-A requesting productId=X will contain Tenant-A's data (or empty), and when Tenant-B hits the same cache key, the stale data is Tenant-A's — however the IAM condition on the original fetch ensures only authorized data enters the cache in the first place, meaning cross-tenant data never materializes in the Lambda's memory.
